speaker: Joshua

comments.flawless: Joshua: The report was right on the first try. Bonus approved.
comments.done: Joshua: Case closed. Next time, check the order against the times first.

all_clues_monologue: That's enough. A fake parcel notice started a program that locked the files, and it spread to the shared folder.
And the offline backup is still safe. Time to press REPORT and put it in order.

entries.title: Parcel notice with a link
entries.detail:
From: notice@track-parc3l.com
To: Marta Silva
Time: 09:12

Your parcel could not be delivered. Click here to choose a new date.
monologue: A parcel notice from track-parc3l, with a 3 where the E should be. A real courier would not hide behind a typo.
That's a real clue.
entries.summary: A fake parcel notice with a link, sent to Marta.

entries.title: "My files look strange"
entries.detail:
From: Marta Silva
To: IT Team
Time: 09:20

All my files have odd endings and there is a note on my screen. I unplugged the cable. What do I do?
monologue: Marta saw the odd endings at 09:20, eight minutes after the parcel notice.
She unplugged the cable. That was smart.
entries.summary: Marta says her files have odd endings and a note.

entries.title: Your order 8821 has shipped
entries.detail:
From: tracking@swiftcourier.com
To: Marta Silva
Time: 08:40

Your order 8821 has shipped. Track it with your account on our site. No need to click anything here.
monologue: A real courier: the right address, a tracking number Marta really ordered, and no link that asks for anything.
Compare it with the other parcel notice and the difference is easy to see.
entries.summary: A real parcel message from a real courier.

entries.title: Month-end reminder
entries.detail:
From: Finance
To: Finance team
Time: 07:55

The month-end report is due on Friday. Please finish your tables.
monologue: A reminder about the month-end report. It explains why Marta is busy, nothing more.
entries.summary: A reminder about the month-end report.

entries.title: Friday lunch menu
entries.detail:
From: Facilities
To: All Staff
Time: 09:05

This Friday's lunch specials are soup and sandwiches.
monologue: Just the lunch menu. Nothing to do with Marta's laptop.
entries.summary: A lunch menu.

entries.title: Parcel notice moved to junk
entries.detail:
From: IT Alerts
To: Dana Pierce
Time: 09:13

A message from track-parc3l.com was moved to your junk folder. It had a link to an unknown site.
monologue: The scanner you turned on caught the same parcel notice for Dana and put it in junk. She never saw it.
entries.summary: The same parcel notice was caught for Dana.

entries.title: "Weird parcel message"
entries.detail:
From: Dana Pierce
To: IT Team
Time: 09:25

I got a parcel message with a link and almost clicked it. Then I heard about Marta. Is it the same one?
monologue: Dana got the same notice and nearly clicked. Without a scanner, it was luck that stopped her.
entries.summary: Dana got the same notice and nearly clicked.

entries.title: 612 files changed in 3 minutes
entries.detail:
Time: 09:15 to 09:18
Where: File server, Finance folder
What happened: 612 files were changed
Started by: Marta's account

Nobody edits 612 files in 3 minutes. A program does.
monologue: 612 files in three minutes, started by Marta's account. No person edits that fast.
A program was doing it. That's a clue.
entries.summary: 612 Finance files changed in 3 minutes, from Marta's account.

entries.title: Backup job renamed files
entries.detail:
Time: 01:00
Where: Backup computer
What happened: Many files were copied and renamed .bak
Started by: Backup Agent

This is the nightly backup. It is approved and runs at 01:00.
monologue: The nightly backup also changes a lot of files, but it does it at 01:00, with its own program.
Many files is not proof.
entries.summary: The nightly backup renames many files at 01:00.

entries.title: One wrong password
entries.detail:
Time: 08:11
Where: Password checker
Who: Dana
What happened: One wrong try, then the right one
monologue: One wrong try, then the right one. People mistype.
entries.summary: Dana mistyped her password once.

entries.title: Updates installed
entries.detail:
Time: 03:00
Where: All laptops
What happened: The monthly updates were installed
monologue: The monthly updates, as announced. Not related.
entries.summary: The monthly updates installed at 03:00.

entries.title: A known hole in the courier's program is closed
entries.detail:
Time: last week
Where: All laptops
What happened: The patch for a known hole in the courier's tracking program was installed
monologue: The updates you kept up to date closed a known hole in the courier's program. One less way in.
entries.summary: The courier's program was patched last week.

entries.title: One laptop was missing a patch
entries.detail:
Time: last week
Where: Marta's laptop
What happened: A patch for a known hole in the courier's tracking program was not installed
monologue: One laptop was missing a patch for a known hole. Marta's. Updates matter.
entries.summary: Marta's laptop was missing a patch.

entries.title: Marta's laptop
entries.detail:
Laptop: Marta's laptop
State: unplugged by Marta at 09:21
Files changed in the first 2 minutes: 42
Last seen on the network: 09:21

Marta pulled the cable herself.
monologue: Marta's laptop changed 42 files in its first two minutes. She unplugged it at 09:21.
entries.summary: Marta's laptop changed 42 files, then she unplugged it.

entries.title: Dana's laptop
entries.detail:
Laptop: Dana's laptop
State: on the network
Files changed: 400, at 10:30
What they were: the Design archive, moved to a new folder
Endings: all normal (.png, .docx)

It looks like a lot of changes, but the files still have their usual endings.
monologue: 400 files changed on Dana's laptop. That looks scary, but the endings are all normal.
She moved the Design archive. Many files is not proof.
entries.summary: Dana moved 400 design files. The endings are normal.

entries.title: Carla's laptop
entries.detail:
Laptop: Carla's laptop
State: on the network
Files changed today: 11
Nothing unusual.
monologue: Nothing unusual on Carla's laptop.
entries.summary: Carla's laptop is fine.

entries.title: Reception laptop
entries.detail:
Laptop: Reception laptop
State: on the network
Files changed today: 3
Nothing unusual.
monologue: Reception is quiet. Nothing to see.
entries.summary: The reception laptop is fine.

entries.title: Backup computer
entries.detail:
Laptop: Backup computer
State: on, the backup drive is unplugged
Files changed today: 0
Nothing unusual.
monologue: The backup computer is fine, and its drive is unplugged.
entries.summary: The backup computer is fine.

entries.title: Offline backup, 01:00
entries.detail:
Time: 01:00
Kept: on a drive that is unplugged after the copy
Checked: yes, it restores fine
Locked files in it: none

Because the drive was not connected, the lock never reached it.
monologue: The offline backup was unplugged right after the copy, so the locks never reached it. It restores fine.
Good news, and a clue about what to do next.
entries.summary: The offline backup from 01:00 is intact and checked.

entries.title: Backup on the shared drive
entries.detail:
Time: 01:00
Kept: on the shared drive, reachable from the network
Checked: no
Locked files in it: yes, the lock reached it at 09:17

A backup that stays connected can be locked too.
monologue: This copy sat on the shared drive, connected to the network. The lock reached it too.
That is why a backup has to be kept apart.
entries.summary: The backup on the shared drive was locked too.

entries.title: Weekly backup, 4 days ago
entries.detail:
Time: four days ago
Kept: on the shared drive
Checked: no

Older, and nobody tested it. It may work, and it may not.
monologue: An old backup, and nobody tested it. It looks safe, but it is not proven.
entries.summary: The weekly backup is old and was never checked.

entries.title: Backup of the design files
entries.detail:
Time: 02:00
Kept: Dana's own drive
Checked: yes

Dana's backup of the Design folder.
monologue: Dana's own backup of her design files. Fine, and not about Finance.
entries.summary: Dana's design backup.

entries.title: Backup schedule
entries.detail:
Job: Backup Agent
Runs: every night at 01:00 and every day at 13:00
From: the file server
To: the backup computer
monologue: When each backup job runs. The nightly one at 01:00 is the one that matters today.
entries.summary: The backup schedule.

entries.title: Finance files renamed .locked
entries.detail:
Time: 09:14
Where: Marta's laptop
What is happening: files are renamed one by one
File: budget_march.xlsx becomes budget_march.xlsx.locked
Then: 41 more, in order

The files cannot be opened any more.
monologue: budget_march.xlsx is now budget_march.xlsx.locked, and 41 more after it, in order.
The files were locked one by one. That's a clue.
entries.summary: Marta's Finance files were renamed .locked.

entries.title: READ_ME.txt
entries.detail:
Time: 09:19
Where: Marta's laptop and the shared Finance folder
What appeared: READ_ME.txt

It says the files are locked and asks for money to open them.
monologue: The note appeared at 09:19, after the files were already locked. It asks for money.
Locking first, asking after.
entries.summary: A note appeared that asks for money.

entries.title: Design archive moved
entries.detail:
Time: 10:30
Where: Dana's laptop
What happened: 400 files were moved to a new folder
Endings: usual ones
monologue: Dana moved a big folder. The endings did not change, so nothing was locked.
entries.summary: Dana moved the Design archive.

entries.title: Onboarding guide
entries.detail:
Time: 08:50
Where: Carla's laptop
What happened: one file changed
monologue: Carla edited a guide. Normal work.
entries.summary: Carla edited a guide.

entries.title: Handbook
entries.detail:
Time: 08:20
Where: File server
What happened: one file changed
monologue: A small edit to the handbook. Not related.
entries.summary: The handbook was edited.

entries.title: Marta's laptop writes to the file server
entries.detail:
Time: 09:15 to 09:18
From: Marta's laptop
Sent to: File server, Finance folder
How much: far more than normal

The lock spread from her laptop into the shared folder.
monologue: The heavy writing went from Marta's laptop straight into the Finance folder. That is how it spread.
entries.summary: Marta's laptop wrote heavily into the Finance folder.

entries.title: Marta's laptop sends one message out
entries.detail:
Time: 09:14
From: Marta's laptop
Sent to: An outside address
How much: one small message

The program phoned home for its key before it locked the files.
monologue: One small message out, just before the files were locked. The program asked its owner for a key.
entries.summary: Marta's laptop sent one small message out.

entries.title: Nightly backup copy
entries.detail:
Time: 01:00
From: File server
Sent to: Backup computer
How much: 9 GB

Approved, and at its usual hour.
monologue: The nightly copy: big, but approved and at its usual hour.
entries.summary: The nightly backup copy.

entries.title: Printer
entries.detail:
Time: 08:30
From: Printer, floor 2
Sent to: File server
How much: small
monologue: The printer sends scans to the file server. Normal.
entries.summary: The printer sent a small scan.

entries.title: Normal web browsing
entries.detail:
Time: all day
From: the laptops
Sent to: websites
How much: usual
monologue: Ordinary web browsing.
entries.summary: Ordinary web browsing.

entries.title: File server
entries.detail:
Computer: File server
Job: Keeps the shared folders
Status: Busy
Busy: 92%, three times its usual load at 09:16
Note: the Finance folder files end in .locked
monologue: The file server is at three times its usual load, and the Finance folder is locked.
entries.summary: The file server was overloaded, with the Finance folder locked.

entries.title: Archive job
entries.detail:
Computer: Archive job
Job: Zips old logs at 08:00
Status: Done
Busy: 40%
Note: many file changes at 08:00, as every day
monologue: Many file changes at 08:00, as every day. Harmless.
entries.summary: The archive job changes many files every day at 08:00.

entries.title: Backup computer
entries.detail:
Computer: Backup computer
Job: Keeps the backups
Status: Running
Busy: 6%
Note: the offline drive was unplugged at 01:20
monologue: The offline drive was unplugged at 01:20. That is why it is intact.
entries.summary: The offline drive was unplugged at 01:20.

entries.title: Mail server
entries.detail:
Computer: Mail server
Job: Receives and sends the company's email
Status: Running
Busy: 28%
monologue: The mail server is running as usual.
entries.summary: The mail server runs as usual.

entries.title: Update server
entries.detail:
Computer: Update server
Job: Sends updates to the laptops
Status: Idle
Busy: 3%
monologue: The update server is idle. Not related.
entries.summary: The update server is idle.

chips.label: Marta clicked the link in the parcel notice (09:12)
it spread to the shared Finance folder (09:16)
the nightly backup ran (01:00)
chips.reason: The nightly backup is real, but it ran eight hours before the attack and is not part of it.

chips.label: Dana moved a big folder (10:30)
chips.reason: Dana's move was ordinary work, and it came after the attack. Her files kept their usual endings.

chips.label: the old weekly backup was checked
chips.reason: Nobody checked the weekly backup. That event never happened.

chips.label: Marta paid the money
chips.reason: Nobody paid. The offline backup made it unnecessary, and paying promises nothing.

report.solved_explanation: This is called ransomware: a harmful program that locks your files, then asks for money to open them. A backup kept apart from the network is what saves you.
report.objective: FINISH THE REPORT BY PUTTING THE EVENTS IN ORDER
